headline: Same few facts, counted several times, make up most of Ward 8's best and worst rankings.
summary:
Three of Ward 8's six worst rankings measure the same absence of coffee. Licensed coffee and tea shops finish 50th in the city's business-license data. A separate Google Maps sweep puts the total shop count and the highly rated subset of it at 49th. Both sources flag their own numbers as thinner than the ranks suggest, with five other wards within two points of the license count and eleven within two points of the Google Maps count. Two more of the worst six describe one fact about language rather than two. A ward with few non-English speakers will score low on any measure of language variety almost by definition, and Ward 8's multilingual and linguistic-diversity scores, both from the same Census survey, land within a point of each other at 49th.

The best six rankings repeat the same pattern, with sturdier sourcing on one pair. Child care shows up twice, once from federal business data and once from the city's own license records, two sources landing on the same conclusion. The other two strongest measures, modeled shares of adults certain God exists and calling their faith strong, come from one statistical model built on the ward's demographics rather than from anyone actually surveyed, and both call themselves low confidence. The clearest number attached to Ward 8 this year sits outside this scorecard entirely. Block Club Chicago reported in July that the ward had more than 580 open tree-cleanup requests after June's storms, the largest backlog anywhere in Chicago, a real count next to a model's guess about how residents feel.
reading_the_rankings: Two rankings are worth a second look. The restaurant count puts Ward 8 at 47th, a rate of 2.15 per 10,000 residents, but twelve other wards are packed within two points of that ranking, and the count itself comes from ZIP code areas rather than ward lines, rated low confidence by its own source. Whatever gap actually separates Ward 8 from its neighbors here, the 47th-place rank overstates it. The modeled certainty-of-God figure runs the other way. The number is precise, 73.9 percent, and the rank is a clean first, but no one in Ward 8 was actually asked. The estimate comes from a model trained on survey respondents elsewhere with similar demographics, projected onto this ward, and its own publisher rates it low confidence too.

news.headline: South Siders Still Waiting For Tree Cleanup After June Storms, But City Departments Are 'Overwhelmed'
news.note: City data showed the 8th Ward had more than 580 open tree-cleanup requests after June storms, the highest total of any Chicago ward.

alderperson.name: Michelle A. Harris
alderperson.verification_note: The website_url listed in the source data, aldermanmichelleharris.net, returned a Cloudflare bot-block on every fetch attempt this session and could not be verified directly. Fetched https://aldermanmichelleharris.com/ instead and confirmed it is her official site, including bio text stating Alderman Harris has lived in the 8th Ward for over fifty years. Cross-checked against the city's official ward page, https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/about/wards/08.html, which lists Alderman Michelle A. Harris for Ward 8, matching the name on file.
